value.rationale: The globally optimal disk theorem motivates a genuine quantitative stability question. Determining all Fourier shape-Hessian eigenvalues, their strict ordering, their translation kernel and the sharp quadrupolar stiffness supplies new nontrivial local information not determined by global maximization, relevant to near-optimal localization domains and constrained perturbations. The result is natural in radius, area and rank, not an arbitrary finite slice; rank two is the first genuinely multieigenvalue case.
